claims.text: The newsroom on the owner's four kinds of device does not agree: each has its own balance, personas, reading list and history, because each is a separate browser.
claims.quote: they do not agree. Each one has its own balance, its own personas, its own reading list and its own history

claims.text: Missing a feature, more than any number on the site, tells the owner the newsroom is going in the right direction.
claims.quote: I miss a feature. And that, more than any number on this site, tells me the newsroom is going in the right direction.

claims.text: The test of whether they miss it applies to the people who build a product, not only to its customers.
claims.quote: it applies to the people who build a product, not only to its customers

claims.text: The most important users are the people building the product and above all those who control the roadmap, because the loop between using and changing is then as short as it can be.
claims.quote: the people building the product, and above all the people who control the roadmap

claims.text: Apple is successful partly because, as far as can be seen from outside, the people there use what they make.
claims.quote: I think this is one of the reasons Apple is so successful.

claims.text: When a product's own team uses something else, or uses it only for the demo, it is a signal the product is not as good as it looks.
claims.quote: When makers do not use what they make, the opposite happens, and it is a signal.

claims.text: The Cyber Boardroom, MyFeeds and early on even sgit as a startup were good ideas the owner was not using, which was the signal he should have listened to.
claims.quote: The Cyber Boardroom, MyFeeds, many of the other things I experimented with, and early on even sgit as a startup.

claims.text: 54 vaults are published on the site with their read keys.
claims.quote: 54 of them are published on this site with their read keys

claims.text: The vaults are getting good not because of a roadmap but because every day the owner hits something and the next release fixes it.
claims.quote: It is because every day I hit something, and the next release fixes it.

claims.text: With agents almost anything can be built; what cannot be generated is the sense of what to build next, for whom, and when to stop, and that comes from using the thing.
claims.quote: What we cannot generate is the sense of what to build next, for whom, and when to stop.

claims.text: The loop is the moat: fast prototyping to production and fast release are what is hard to copy, much harder than any single feature.
claims.quote: Fast prototyping to production, and fast release, is what is hard to copy, much harder than any single feature.

claims.text: A reading list made for one person went from brief to live in 81 minutes; a link to a persona in 17 hours.
claims.quote: a reading list made for one person went from brief to live in 81 minutes

claims.text: Build the reader's own encrypted vault so the newsroom is the same on every device, with nothing on a server of ours, no account database and no password.
claims.quote: Nothing on a server of ours, no account database, no password.

claims.text: An access key for the vault server, pasted on the account page, kept in the browser's storage for the site, never in a URL, removable in one tap.
claims.quote: The reader pastes it on the account page; it is kept in the browser's storage for this site, never put in a URL, and removable in one tap.

claims.text: A key pair for the reader, generated in the browser with Web Crypto with a non-extractable private key, the first real use of RFC 0001 on the newsroom.
claims.quote: This is the first real use of RFC 0001 on the newsroom.

claims.text: One log per device, appended as events and never edited by another device; state is computed from every log, and the merge is a union with no conflicts.
claims.quote: Two devices that were offline both write their own logs, and the merge is a union: no conflicts to resolve.

claims.text: Receipts are counted once by their payment reference, so a top-up made on one device appears on the others and is not credited twice.
claims.quote: Receipts are counted once, by their payment reference

claims.text: Add a device first by a code on screen carrying the vault key and access key; next a passkey on secrets.sgit.ai's design, and sign-in with Google that says who you are but holds no key.
claims.quote: a passkey that unlocks the keys, on the design of secrets.sgit.ai, so the reader does not handle a key at all

claims.text: A one-way line to the agent that edits the site: a note marked to the newsroom is encrypted in the browser to the desk's published key and dropped into a write-only lane.
claims.quote: It is encrypted in the browser to the desk's published key

claims.text: The vault server sees ciphertext, its size and when it is written, not what you read; a script on the site could see everything, so the newsroom loads no third-party scripts.
claims.quote: What the vault server sees: ciphertext, its size, and when it is written. Not what you read.

claims.text: The real test of the feature is that the owner uses it on four devices for a week and stops missing it.
claims.quote: I use it, on four devices, for a week, and I stop missing it.

claims.text: What not to build: no account database, no server endpoint, no email and password, nothing that sends the vault key anywhere, no sync of anything not done on purpose.
claims.quote: No account database, no server endpoint of ours, no email and password, nothing that sends the vault key anywhere

claims.text: One user is not a market: the owner is the first user and best placed to feel the gap, but that is a direction, not proof others will want it.
claims.quote: One user is not a market.

claims.text: The past is the owner's own account; why his earlier startups did not take off is more than one reason, and not using them is the one he can see most clearly.
claims.quote: The past is my own account of it.

claims.text: None of the vault feature is built; the brief is a design, and the pieces it builds on exist.
claims.quote: The brief is a design; the pieces it builds on exist.

claims.text: The article comes from a voice memo of 11 October 2026 after a day reading the newsroom on four devices; the times are from the git logs of both sites.
claims.quote: The times in the second are from the git logs of this site and of the newsroom.
